content.title: Water Restrictions
content.summary: The City has declared a drought and implemented Stage 1 water restrictions effective April 15, 2026, mandating limited outdoor watering to two assigned days per week and a goal of reducing water use by approximately 20%. Additionally, the City Council will vote on proposed drought surcharges for residential and irrigation customers at the June 16 meeting, which, if approved, would take effect on July 1, 2026. The surcharges aim to encourage water conservation during the drought, with rates increasing based on water usage.
content.body:
The City receives the majority of its water supply from Denver Water. We are contractually required to follow drought related water shortage restrictions in line with Denver Water. This includes a 4-staged approach to watering restrictions as detailed below.

## Current restrictions

Updated 6/4/26

**The City has declared a drought and Stage 1 water restrictions are effective April 15, 2026.**For more detailed information, review the [full set of rules and regulations](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=8f8a11836c23b).

Watering restrictions align with the direction of Denver Water and are subject to change.

—

**The City is proposing drought surcharges for single-family residential and irrigation only water customers.**City Council will vote on the drought surcharges at the **June 16 Council meeting.**

Drought surcharges are a tool for encouraging water conservation during drought. Surcharges help signal the additional value of water during this time of drought.

In addition to [existing rates](/460)[,](//arvadaco.gov/utilitiesrates,) the proposed bi-monthly drought surcharge for single-family residential customers is:

- 0 - 12,000 gallons: $0 / 1,000 gallons (unchanged to cover reasonable indoor use)
- 12,001 - 30,000 gallons: $1.10 / 1,000 gallons
- Above 30,000 gallons: $2.20 / 1,000 gallons

For irrigation only accounts, the proposed drought surcharge is $2.20 / 1,000 gallons for all water use.

If passed, the surcharges would be **effective July 1, 2026**.

## Stage 1: Mandatory restrictions, limited outdoor watering

Stage 1 means water supply is low and mandatory restrictions are in place. The goal is to reduce water use by approximately 20%.

### Outdoor watering

- Limited lawn watering to**two assigned days per week** based on schedule (see below)
- **No watering 10am to 6pm**
- Cycle sprinkler run times to 5 minutes, watering 15 minutes max per zone (visit the [watering tips webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/597) for more tips like this)
- Trees, shrubs, perennials, vegetable gardens, and flowers can be watered any day using a handheld hose or drip irrigation, outside of 10am to 6pm
- New grass seed or sod installation is subject to the 2-day watering schedule from June through August
- Do not waste water by letting it spray on concrete and asphalt or pool in gutters, streets, and alleys
- Repair leaking sprinkler systems in a timely manner
- Do not irrigate during rain or high winds

| Customer type | Assigned lawn watering days |
| --- | --- |
| Single-family residential: **even-numbered addresses**(ex. 5560) | Sunday and Thursday |
| Single-family residential: **odd-numbered addresses**(ex. 5561) | Wednesday and Saturday |
| **All others** (including multifamily, commercial, and HOA common areas) | Tuesday and Friday |

The assigned lawn watering days listed here are correct. A limited number of customers received information printed with the incorrect days.

### Pools, water features, and car washing

- Encouraged not to operate outdoor fountains or water features that spray water into the air
- Car washing at home with a bucket or handheld hose with shut-off nozzle
- Power washing limited to assigned watering days
- Swimming pools can be filled

### Parks, athletic fields, and golf courses

- Follow mandatory watering schedule, reduce water use by 20%, or utilize a designated water budget
- [Learn more about how the City's two golf courses, West Woods and Lake Arbor, are following restrictions](/634)

### Businesses

- Restaurants only serve water upon request
- Lodging facilities limit changing sheets to upon request or for health and safety reasons
- Commercial car washes must follow best practices for no water waste
- Fleet vehicle washing limited to once per week except for health and safety reasons
- Commercial power washing is allowed when essential to business operations

## Learn More

Listen to the Inside Arvada podcast episode with Water Supply Administrator Amy Willhite discussing drought conditions and water restrictions. Use the player below or wherever you listen to podcasts, including [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/19034579)(with transcript).

## Other Stages

1. [Watch](#tab2ae08c0c-4981-4d6d-8e2d-96df4d8e2347_0)

## Watch: Voluntary restrictions

A watch means water supplies are below average and conditions are dry. Continued dry weather could lead to mandatory restrictions.

### Outdoor watering

- Follow [best practices for outdoor watering](/597): water no more than 3 days a week, outside of 10am to 6pm
- Look for ways to reduce water use
- Fix leaking sprinklers and faucets
- Avoid letting water run into gutters, streets, and pavement
- Do not water during rain or high winds

### Restaurants

- Consider only serving water upon request

1. [Stage 2](#tab2ae08c0c-4981-4d6d-8e2d-96df4d8e2347_1)

## Stage 2: Increased restrictions, lawn irrigation prohibited

Stage 2 means the drought is severe. Restrictions increase and landscape damage is possible. The goal is to reduce water use by approximately 35%. 

### Outdoor watering

- Lawn watering is not allowed
- Trees and shrubs may be watered once a week on assigned day using a handheld hose or drip irrigation, outside of 10am to 6pm
- Vegetable gardens may be watered using a handheld hose or drip irrigation, outside of 10am to 6pm
- No new grass, sod, trees, shrubs, flowers, or vegetables may be planted

### Pools, water features, and car washing

- Outdoor fountains and water features prohibited
- Single-family residential pools cannot be filled or refilled (community pools may continue operating)
- Car washing at home is not allowed

### Parks, athletic fields, and golf courses

- Follow strict mandatory watering schedule or water budget

### Businesses

- Restaurants required to only serve water upon request
- Lodging facilities have mandatory laundry restrictions
- Construction water use must follow best practices for no water waste
- Only commercial car washed using recycled water may operate
- Fleet vehicle washing limited to once per month for health and safety only

1. [Stage 3](#tab2ae08c0c-4981-4d6d-8e2d-96df4d8e2347_2)

## Stage 3: Water rationing

Stage 3 is unlikely. If conditions become extreme, stage 3 requires water rationing. The goal is to reduce water use by approximately 50%. 

All of the restrictions from earlier stages but to a stricter degree. Indoor water use may be restricted, swimming pools closed, and only car washes using recycled water allowed. Water is prioritized for essential indoor and public safety uses.

### [FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=107)

[What are the current water restrictions in Arvada?](#)
:   Arvada is under Stage 1 drought restrictions, which include mandatory limits on outdoor watering. Lawn watering should be limited to two days per week on your assigned days:

    - Single family homes with **even**-numbered addresses: **Sunday and Thursday**
    - Single family homes with **odd**-numbered addresses: **Wednesday and Saturday**
    - All other customers (including multifamily and commercial properties): **Tuesday and Friday**

    For a complete list of restrictions and additional resources, visit the [**watering restrictions webpage**](/1499).

[When do water restrictions take effect, and how long will they last?](#)
:   Restrictions take effect April 15, 2026 and may be in place for a full calendar year. The City will continue to monitor drought conditions and evaluate the ability to remove restrictions sooner or the need to extend restrictions longer.

[Can I water my trees and garden?](#)
:   Yes. Under Stage 1 restrictions, trees, shrubs, perennials, annuals, and gardens can be watered any day by hand-held hose or drip irrigation before 10am or after 6pm.

[What happens if I don’t follow restrictions?](#)
:   The City will be issuing warning notices and fines to customers who are out of compliance as follows:

    1. First violation: warning notice
    2. Second violation: $100 fine added to the water bill
    3. Third violation: $250 fine added to the water bill
    4. Fourth violation: $500 fine added to the water bill

[What resources are available to help me conserve water?](#)
:   The City has a variety of resources to help customers reduce water use:

    - [Resource Central](http://resourcecentral.org) free and low-cost programs to help save water outdoors.
    - [Outdoor watering tips](/597) provide practical guidance for improving irrigation efficiency and maintaining a healthy landscape with less water.
    - [EyeOnWater](/835) is a free tool being rolled out to customers to track their water use in near-real time, set leak alerts, and identify unusual usage patterns. This technology is still being installed and not yet available to all customers. If your water meter has a black plastic lid you are likely able to join the program.
    - [Indoor leak detection tips](/1505) can help find and fix leaks that can waste water.

[Why is the City watering at parks, golf courses, and athletic fields when I’m being told to cut back?](#)
:   The City follows restrictions and maintains drought plans to reduce water use across our parks, golf courses, athletic fields, and public spaces. Athletic fields and golf courses use non-potable water where possible and are prioritized for watering based on community use. These areas have functional grass that requires a higher level of maintenance to ensure safe function and playability. We offset prioritized areas like golf courses and athletic fields by further reducing water use in other spaces like non-functional grass at parks. This ensures Parks and Golf still reach the 20% water use reduction goal. You may see more brown areas in some public spaces, this is by design, not neglect.

[Why is the City watering in the middle of the day?](#)
:   While the City makes every effort to water before 10am and after 6pm, there are a few reasons crews may be turning on irrigation during their regular working hours.

    - Occasionally crews need to perform manual, visual checks on irrigation lines, particularly at the beginning of the season. In order to inspect lines, Parks team members run irrigation systems during regular working hours.
    - Athletic field programming may require some day time irrigation of infields to manage the demand on the system and allow for consistent, safe playing conditions.

[Why is the Olde Town Fountain not running full time but the Splash Pad at Ralston Central Park is?](#)
:   The Splash Pad uses water that is captured, treated, recycled, and used again similar to a swimming pool. This means we can run the Splash Pad and still meet our water conservation goals. The Olde Town Fountain is tied into the regular water and sewer system and the water cannot be recycled. This means when it is running we continue to use more water. Running it full time would hinder our ability to reduce water use by 20% this year. During Stage 1 restrictions, the Olde Town fountain will run on a limited basis for special events like the Farmer’s Market and Second Saturdays.

[Why do City parks water outside of the assigned days?](#)
:   The City maintains over 100 parks. There would be too much demand on the system to water all parks on the same two days of the week. Instead, parks monitor water use to ensure a 20% water reduction. Parks will be watered outside of 10am to 6pm, unless performing maintenance. Other City facilities, like City Hall and the police stations follow the assigned 2-day per week schedule.

[My neighbor is not following the water restrictions, what should I do?](#)
:   Consider connecting with your neighbors directly. It is possible that they are unaware they are violating the rules. If the behavior continues, you may [report waste of water through Ask Arvada](/898).

[Can I plant and water a new Garden in a Box or other low-water garden?](#)
:   Yes. However, watering restrictions still apply. New plantings are allowed when watered by hand or drip irrigation. Watering must take place outside of 10am to 6pm.

[Can I plant new grass sod or seed?](#)
:   Yes, this is allowed in Stage 1. However, it is recommended that you do not plant new grass from June through August as you will be required to follow your assigned watering day schedule. New grass seed or sod planting is not allowed in later stages of restrictions.

[Can I fill my swimming pool during drought restrictions?](#)
:   During Stage 1 restrictions, swimming pools can be filled. There are additional restrictions on swimming pools in later stages of drought restrictions.

[Are some properties exempt from watering restrictions?](#)
:   Not if they are using City of Arvada water. Some properties in Arvada rely on ditch or well water and they are not serviced by the City. These properties are not required to follow the City’s restrictions.

    Some properties have an approved [City variance](/1518) if they meet specific criteria. These properties are still expected to reduce water use by 20% but may have a variance on how they meet that requirement.

[Can I appeal a water restrictions violation?](#)
:   If you have received a water restrictions violation from the City, you may submit an appeal. The following requirements apply to the appeals process:

    - Submit within 30 days of receiving the violation.
    - Submit a reason for the appeal.
    - A hearing will be scheduled with the City of Arvada.

    [File a water restrictions violation appeal.](https://arvada.form.transform.civicplus.com/64676)

[Are restrictions related to rate increases?](#)
:   These are separate issues. Annual rate increases support the ongoing operation, maintenance, repair, and replacement of utilities infrastructure. Much of which was built between the 1960s and 1980s and is at or near the end of its useful life. Drought restrictions are about lower than normal water supply due to an extremely dry winter.

    In drought years or not, the rates you pay continue to fund utilities operations to maintain clean, reliable drinking water service for the public health and safety of our community.

[Is Arvada running out of water?](#)
:   No. Arvada is in a very good position with water supply in normal years. This year’s restrictions are a response to one of the driest winters on record with very limited snowpack.

[Is it possible that the City would move to a higher stage of drought and restrictions?](#)
:   This is a possibility. Drought conditions can evolve throughout the course of the year. The City aligns with Denver Water’s drought stages. If Denver Water moves to a higher drought stage, the City will do the same. The City would update the rules for a new drought stage with an updated effective date.

[Is the City implementing drought pricing on outdoor water use?](#)
:   The City is proposing drought pricing for single-family residential units, irrigation only accounts, and other individually connected units. Drought pricing will require approval from City Council and would go into effect in July or later this summer. Drought pricing will remain in effect as long as the City remains in a drought declaration.

    Multifamily units and other multi-unit properties like shopping centers will not be subject to surcharges. The intention is focused on properties with significant outdoor water use.

/FAQ.aspx
